name: 01_coast_west
what: the W coast: the plateau, the shingle beach falling to the shore ice, the first sea cliffs

name: 02_wreck_beach
what: the wreck heeled into ragged shore-fast ice at the beach foot (no rectangle, R-C9-228)

name: 03_cliffs_south
what: the S sea cliffs (6-8 m): rock-kit columns, talus, a stack in the shore-fast ice

name: 04_cove_close
what: CLOSE: the cave worn into the cliff face at the waterline, the stair in a natural gully beside it (R-C9-228)

name: 05_cave_mouth
what: the cave mouth: a dark tide-worn arch in the face, 7 m clear, sea and floes at its mouth, a small iced ledge

name: 06_mere
what: the mere (~440 m2): mostly continuous ice, a few long branching cracks, reed islands (R-C9-227)

name: 07_pack_ice
what: the sea: irregular pack -- huge and tiny plates, rubble zones, leads of every width (~2/3 ice, R-C9-227)

name: 08_start
what: the start in the stone circle (4 standing, 2 fallen low blocks)

name: 09_stair_close
what: CLOSE: the stair -- every tread its own stone (snow on top, bare stone at the front), 5 m clear, climbing inland

name: 10_cove_wide
what: WIDE: the continuous cliff line -- the cave in the face, the stair gully between rock columns

name: 11_mere_sea
what: the mere turning into the sea: irregular cracks widening westward into leads and rubble, reed islands (R-C9-229)

name: 12_river_mere
what: the river: a tiny UN-FROZEN ribbon of open water down the coast into the mere's ice (R-C9-227)

name: 13_hall_yard
what: the burnt hall's ash yard: an irregular trampled patch, no straight edges
